summary: Lit in 1875 at the end of Ontonagon's west pier. A storm carried the first tower away in 1899; the 1900 iron beacon still stands, closed to visitors.

light.fog_signal: Electric siren in the iron tower from 1933, replacing a hand fog signal

lens.note: The 1900 fixed red light was of the fourth order (LHB FY1901). LighthouseFriends says a plastic beacon later took the place of a fourth-order Fresnel lens.

structures.type: square pyramidal steel frame with watch room
structures.note: 26 feet 10 inches (8.2 m) to the focal plane, per the Board's FY1901 report. Solar LED light since 2013.
Carried away in a storm on 12 December 1899.

staffing.note: The pierhead had no keeper of its own; its beacon was given to the keeper of the main Ontonagon light (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Tower closed (LighthouseFriends). The US Lighthouse Society record says the station is not open to the public.

visit.note: LighthouseFriends suggests viewing it from the main Ontonagon light or from the beach on the river's east side.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (owner per LighthouseFriends; GSA auction offers 2019 and 2024)

events.note: Lit for the first time on 20 September 1875, about 200 feet from the outer end of the west pier
Moved 535 feet lakeward as the pier was extended
Moved 865 feet lakeward; a 767-foot elevated walkway built atop the pier
Iron gallery placed round the lantern so the keeper could clean the glass
Moved 378 feet nearer the outer end of the pier on 30 September 1893 (Board). LighthouseFriends gives roughly 400 feet.
Open framework tower carried away in a severe storm, 12 December 1899
Temporary fixed red light shown from a wooden house with a square lantern, night of 16 April 1900
Iron beacon delivered 31 July 1900; its fixed red light of the fourth order shown 10 November 1900
Damaged in the Great Lakes storm of 8-10 November 1913; the Bulletin gives about $4,000 for the group of stations named
Electric siren established in the iron tower, replacing a hand fog signal
Made available under the National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act on 15 May 2012; county historical society applied; transfer did not occur (LighthouseFriends)
Solar-powered LED light replaced a plastic beacon
GSA public auction, starting bid $5,000; high bid $7,500 on 17 September 2019; LighthouseFriends infers the winner did not complete the purchase
GSA offered the lighthouse again under the NHLPA in June 2024

notes_for_editor: 1) No keeper roster exists for the pierhead on USLHS (roster.py prints ROSTER: none listed for showPeople/7103). The only keeper a source names at the pierhead is James Corgan, in 1910 (LighthouseFriends). USLHS lists him as principal keeper of the MAIN light 1883-1919; Thomas Stripe (1864-1883) kept the main light before him. No source ties anyone to the pierhead beacon in 1875-1883, so those years have no named keeper. 2) The 1875, 1879, 1884 and 1889 events rest on LighthouseFriends alone. The corpus holds Lighthouse Board volumes for 1891-1901 only. 3) The 1909 letter (Calumet News, 13 Dec 1909, reprinting the Ontonagon Herald) is dated Washington, 3 Dec 1909, and signed 'Jams Corgan' in the OCR. It gives no office and the story does not link it to the keeper. LighthouseFriends' 1909 reply to the Corps of Engineers is by James Corgan as village president; that reply was not read in the Corps' own file. The OCR of the Calumet page is poor; the spelling of the signature is unconfirmed. 4) Main light dates disagree: established 1852 (USLHS) against 1853 (LighthouseFriends); discontinued 1963 (LighthouseFriends) against 1964 (USLHS; optic removed 1964). The story states both. 5) Scan page numbers are cited because printed page numbers were not confirmed for the Board volumes (FY1894 scan p.524 and FY1901 scan p.236 were checked against the corpus page index). 6) The pierhead's 2024 status is from LighthouseFriends, whose page is undated; no later ownership source was found. Current ownership is unverified. 7) Coordinates: the record uses 46.879467, -89.330844 (LighthouseFriends). USLHS gives 46 deg 52' 47" N, 89 deg 19' 30" W, to the minute only. Not changed. 8) The record's fog_signal 'horn' does not match LighthouseFriends' 1933 electric siren; unchecked. 9) Excluded: LSS entries for a steamer named Ontonagon (1881, 1882) and Fourteen Mile Point. 10) Chronicling America searches for the 1875 lighting and the 1899 storm returned no relevant pages. 11) Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1963/1964 disagreement is now stated in the text; the letter is no longer used to identify the keeper; the 1893, 1899-1900 and 1901 Board-report pages were confirmed against the corpus page index.
